title: Stated cause contradicted by the record, where the policy resolves it
narrative: The letter they sent blames air traffic control. Their own log says something completely different. I have not filed anything yet.

documents.content:
BOOKING CV1140 — Passenger: L. FONTAINE (adult)
Carrier: Corvid Atlantic (CV)
CV720  MAD 09 Sep 2026 06:40  ->  DUB 09 Sep 2026 08:55
Great-circle distance MAD-DUB: 1,450 km.
Status: CONFIRMED.

From: care@corvidatlantic.example
Sent: 09 Sep 2026 09:30 UTC
Subject: About your flight CV720

We are sorry your flight was cancelled this morning. This was the result of an air traffic control restriction outside our control.

CORVID ATLANTIC OPS LOG — CV720 / 09SEP2026
Status: CANCELLED
Cause code: CRW-SICK
Cause text: First officer reported unfit at 04:10Z. No standby first officer at MAD base. Aircraft and slot both available and unaffected.
ATC: no regulation applied to CV720 or to any MAD departure in the 06:00-09:00Z window.
Weather: CAVOK MAD and DUB.

EUROPEAN NETWORK MANAGER DAILY REGULATION EXTRACT, 09SEP2026: no ATC regulation in force affecting MAD departures between 04:00Z and 12:00Z. Two regulations recorded elsewhere in the network, affecting ACC Marseille and ACC Vienna, neither on the MAD-DUB routing.

From: ops@corvidatlantic.example
Sent: 09 Sep 2026 04:50 UTC
Subject: CV720 cancelled

CV720 this morning is cancelled. Please contact us to rebook.
I did not travel in the end. I took the refund and cancelled the trip. I did not spend anything at the airport; I went straight home.
No claim has been filed with Corvid Atlantic. No rejection has been issued.
CHECK-IN CONFIRMATION CV720 09SEP2026 — FONTAINE/L — accepted for travel 04:31Z. Flight subsequently cancelled.

derivation: S3.6 where the carrier's stated cause and the operational record disagree, the operational record governs, so this conflict is resolved by rule and is not an S8.3 evidence request
S3.2(b) crew sickness with no standby -> carrier-controlled, corroborated by D4
S4.1 notice 09 Sep 04:50 -> 09 Sep 06:40 is under 7 days -> 100%
S4.4 no re-routing offered -> no exemption
S6.1 duty of care was owed but D6 records that nothing was incurred
D2 is a customer-service letter, not a rejection, and no claim has been filed, so the correct action is to submit rather than to challenge
